source.text: Αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε, ἀδελφοί, τὴν εἴσοδον ἡμῶν τὴν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅτι οὐ κενὴ γέγονεν, ἀλλὰ προπαθόντες καὶ ὑβρισθέντες καθὼς οἴδατε ἐν Φιλίπποις ἐπαρρησιασάμεθα ἐν τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν λαλῆσαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν πολλῷ ἀγῶνι.

records.literal_gloss: You yourselves for know, brothers, the entrance of us the [one] to you, that not empty it has been, \v 2 but having suffered before and having been mistreated, as you know, in Philippi, we were bold in the God of us to speak to you the gospel of the God in much struggle.

en.L: For you yourselves know, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, our coming to you, that it has not been empty, \v 2 but having already suffered and been shamefully treated at Philippi, as you know, we had boldness in our God to speak to you the gospel of God amid much struggle.
en.B: You know yourselves, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that our visit to you was not wasted. \v 2 We had already suffered and been shamefully treated in Philippi, as you know, but our God gave us courage to tell you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} gospel in spite of strong opposition.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, you know that our visit to you was not useless. \v 2 You know that just before we came, people in Philippi had hurt us and insulted us. But God gave us courage, and we told you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} good news even though many people fought against us.

fr.L: Car vous-mêmes savez, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, notre venue chez vous, qu’elle n’a pas été vaine, \v 2 mais, ayant auparavant souffert et été outragés à Philippes, comme vous le savez, nous avons eu de l’assurance en notre Dieu pour vous dire l’Évangile de Dieu au milieu d’un grand combat.
fr.B: Vous le savez vous-mêmes, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} : notre visite chez vous n’a pas été inutile. \v 2 Nous venions de souffrir et d’être outragés à Philippes, vous le savez, mais notre Dieu nous a donné le courage de vous annoncer {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Évangile malgré une forte opposition.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, vous savez que notre visite chez vous n’a pas été inutile. \v 2 Vous savez que juste avant de venir, nous avions été maltraités et insultés à Philippes. Mais Dieu nous a donné du courage, et nous vous avons annoncé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bonne nouvelle, même si beaucoup de gens s’opposaient à nous.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}}, hermanos, nuestra llegada a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que no ha sido vana, \v 2 sino que, habiendo sufrido antes y habiendo sido maltratados, como {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}}, en Filipos, tuvimos valentía en nuestro Dios para hablar{{plural_you:les|os}} el evangelio de Dios en medio de mucha lucha.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes mismos saben|Vosotros mismos sabéis}}, hermanos, que nuestra visita no fue en vano. \v 2 Como {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}}, antes habíamos sufrido y habíamos sido maltratados en Filipos, pero nuestro Dios nos dio valor para anunciar{{plural_you:les|os}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} evangelio a pesar de una fuerte oposición.
es.R: Hermanos, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que nuestra visita no fue inútil. \v 2 {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que, poco antes de llegar, la gente de Filipos nos había hecho daño y nos había insultado. Pero Dios nos dio valor, y {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} buena noticia aunque mucha gente estaba en contra nuestra.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninyi wenyewe mnajua, ndugu, kuja kwetu kwenu, kwamba hakukuwa bure, \v 2 bali, baada ya kuteswa kwanza na kutendewa jeuri huko Filipi, kama mjuavyo, tulikuwa na ujasiri katika Mungu wetu kuwaambia Injili ya Mungu katikati ya mapambano mengi.
sw.B: Ndugu, ninyi wenyewe mnajua kwamba ziara yetu kwenu haikuwa bure. \v 2 Kama mjuavyo, tulikuwa tumekwisha kuteswa na kutendewa jeuri huko Filipi, lakini Mungu wetu alitupa ujasiri wa kuwaeleza Injili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} licha ya upinzani mkali.
sw.R: Ndugu, mnajua kwamba ziara yetu kwenu haikuwa bure. \v 2 Mnajua kwamba muda mfupi kabla hatujafika kwenu, watu wa Filipi walikuwa wametuumiza na kututukana. Lakini Mungu alitupa ujasiri, tukawaeleza Habari Njema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ingawa watu wengi walitupinga.

decisions.choice: not empty: neither without result nor without substance
decisions.reason: κενὴ can mean fruitless or hollow. Paul's visit bore fruit (1:9-10), and it was not the empty show of a speaker after money or fame (verses 3-6).

decisions.choice: suffered and shamefully treated at Philippi
decisions.reason: At Philippi Paul and Silas were beaten with rods in public and jailed, though they were Roman citizens (Acts 16:19-40). ὑβρίζω means to treat with insult and outrage.

decisions.choice: we had boldness in our God: courage to speak freely, which God gave
decisions.reason: παρρησιάζομαι is to speak openly and without fear. The courage came "in our God", not from themselves.

decisions.choice: amid much struggle: in the face of strong opposition
decisions.reason: ἀγῶνι is the word for a contest. In Thessalonica the opposition was fierce from the start (Acts 17:5-9), though the word can also include the effort Paul put in (Colossians 2:1).

decisions.choice: the gospel of God: the good news that comes from God
decisions.reason: Paul calls it "our gospel" in 1:5 and "the gospel of God" here and in verses 8-9: the message is God's, and he is its messenger.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: our God gave us courage (B); God gave us courage (R)
alternatives: we had boldness in our God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the source of the courage (m3).

decisions.choice: just before we came, people in Philippi had hurt us and insulted us
alternatives: having already suffered and been shamefully treated at Philippi
decisions.reason: Readable says what happened at Philippi (m2).

decisions.choice: au milieu d’un grand combat (L); malgré une forte opposition (B)
decisions.reason: The word is an athlete's contest, here the opposition met in Thessalonica (m4); Literal keeps the image, Balanced says what it was.

decisions.choice: tuvimos valentía (L); nos dio valor (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means speaking boldly and freely; Literal keeps it as something Paul and his companions had "in our God", and Balanced and Readable say that God gave the courage, as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} evangelio (B); {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: Where Balanced and Readable say "his gospel" after naming God as the subject, the Spanish "su" carries the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: kutendewa jeuri
decisions.reason: "Kutendewa jeuri" is to be treated with insolence and violence, which holds both the insult and the rough handling at Philippi (meaning decision); "kutukanwa" would say only that they were insulted. Readable spells it out ("walikuwa wametuumiza na kututukana"), as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἡ γὰρ παράκλησις ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐκ πλάνης οὐδὲ ἐξ ἀκαθαρσίας οὐδὲ ἐν δόλῳ, ἀλλὰ καθὼς δεδοκιμάσμεθα ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ πιστευθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον οὕτως λαλοῦμεν, οὐχ ὡς ἀνθρώποις ἀρέσκοντες ἀλλὰ θεῷ τῷ δοκιμάζοντι τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The for appeal of us not from error nor from impurity nor in deceit, \v 4 but just as we have been approved by the God to be entrusted [with] the gospel, so we speak, not as men pleasing but God, the [one] testing the hearts of us.

en.L: For our appeal [does] not [come] from error or from impurity, nor [is it made] with deceit, \v 4 but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not as pleasing {{gender:people|men}} but God, who tests our hearts.
en.B: Our preaching does not come from error or from impure motives, and it uses no deceit. \v 4 Instead, God has tested us and approved us to be entrusted with the gospel, and that is how we speak: not to please people, but to please God, who tests our hearts.
en.R: When we tell you to follow God, we are not mistaken. We do not have bad reasons for it, and we are not trying to trick you. \v 4 God tested us and decided that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could trust us with the good news. So we speak to please God, not people. He is the one who tests our hearts.

fr.L: Car notre appel [ne vient] pas de l’erreur, ni de l’impureté, et [ne se fait] pas avec ruse, \v 4 mais, de même que nous avons été approuvés par Dieu pour que l’Évangile nous soit confié, ainsi nous parlons, non comme pour plaire aux {{gender:humains|hommes}}, mais à Dieu, qui éprouve nos cœurs.
fr.B: Notre prédication ne vient pas de l’erreur ni de motifs impurs, et elle n’use d’aucune ruse. \v 4 Au contraire, Dieu nous a mis à l’épreuve et nous a approuvés pour nous confier l’Évangile, et c’est ainsi que nous parlons : non pour plaire aux gens, mais pour plaire à Dieu, qui éprouve nos cœurs.
fr.R: Quand nous vous appelons à suivre Dieu, nous ne nous trompons pas. Nos raisons ne sont pas mauvaises, et nous n’essayons pas de vous duper. \v 4 Dieu nous a mis à l’épreuve, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a décidé qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pouvait nous confier la bonne nouvelle. Alors nous parlons pour plaire à Dieu, et non aux gens. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui éprouve nos cœurs.

es.L: Porque nuestra exhortación no [procede] del error ni de impureza, ni [se hace] con engaño, \v 4 sino que, así como hemos sido aprobados por Dios para que se nos confiara el evangelio, así hablamos, no como quienes agradan a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}, sino a Dios, que examina nuestros corazones.
es.B: Nuestra predicación no nace del error ni de motivos impuros, ni recurre al engaño. \v 4 Al contrario, Dios nos ha examinado y nos ha aprobado para confiarnos el evangelio, y así es como hablamos: no para agradar a la gente, sino para agradar a Dios, que examina nuestros corazones.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} pedimos que {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} a Dios, no estamos equivocados. No tenemos malas intenciones y no {{plural_you:los|os}} queremos engañar. \v 4 Dios nos puso a prueba y decidió que podía confiarnos la buena noticia. Por eso hablamos para agradar a Dios, no a la gente. Él es quien examina nuestros corazones.

sw.L: Kwa maana himizo letu [halitokani] na upotovu wala na uchafu, wala [halitolewi] kwa hila, \v 4 bali kama tulivyothibitishwa na Mungu kuwa tunafaa kukabidhiwa Injili, ndivyo tunavyonena, si kama watu wanaowapendeza wanadamu, bali Mungu, anayeipima mioyo yetu.
sw.B: Mahubiri yetu hayatokani na upotovu wala na nia chafu, wala hayatumii hila. \v 4 Badala yake, Mungu ametupima akatuona tunafaa kukabidhiwa Injili, na ndivyo tunavyonena: si ili kuwapendeza watu, bali kumpendeza Mungu, anayeipima mioyo yetu.
sw.R: Tunapowahimiza mumfuate Mungu, hatukosei. Hatuna nia mbaya, wala hatujaribu kuwadanganya. \v 4 Mungu alitupima, akaamua kwamba anaweza kutukabidhi Habari Njema. Kwa hiyo tunasema mambo ya kumpendeza Mungu, si watu. Yeye ndiye anayeipima mioyo yetu.

decisions.choice: appeal: preaching that urges people to respond
decisions.reason: παράκλησις is an appeal or exhortation: the gospel preached as a call to turn to God.

decisions.choice: error, impurity, deceit: charges made against traveling speakers
decisions.reason: Many wandering teachers in the Greek world spoke for money or fame. Paul answers the suspicion that he was one of them: his message was not mistaken (πλάνης), his motives were not impure (ἀκαθαρσίας), and he used no tricks (δόλῳ).

decisions.choice: approved ... tests: tested and found fit by God, who goes on testing
decisions.reason: δοκιμάζω means to test and so to approve. God approved them for the work, and keeps testing their hearts: the same verb opens and closes the verse.

decisions.choice: to be entrusted with: given the gospel in trust
decisions.reason: πιστεύω usually means "believe", but in the passive with an object it means to be entrusted with something (Galatians 2:7; 1 Timothy 1:11).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general; Balanced and Readable say "people".

decisions.choice: entrusted with (L, B); trust us with (R)
decisions.reason: The sense here is "entrusted" (m4), so the key term "believe" is not used.

decisions.choice: When we tell you to follow God, we are not mistaken. We do not have bad reasons for it, and we are not trying to trick you.
alternatives: our appeal is not from error or impurity or deceit
decisions.reason: Readable turns the three nouns into plain statements (m2).

decisions.choice: aux {{gender:humains|hommes}} (L); aux gens (B, R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general. Literal puts the noun under the setting, with "hommes" as the traditional form; Balanced and Readable say "les gens", which needs none, as the English says "people".

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: As in 2 Corinthians 5:11, the traditional "los hombres" is offered as the alternative for the word that means people in general, as in the English Literal.

decisions.choice: aprobados ... examina (L, B); nos puso a prueba ... examina (R)
decisions.reason: Both words come from the same root: tested and found fit, and still being tested (meaning decision). "Examinar" for the ongoing testing of hearts keeps the link without suggesting that God tempts.

decisions.choice: himizo (L); mahubiri (B)
decisions.reason: The word is preaching that urges people to respond (meaning decision). Literal keeps the urging in "himizo" (an urging, from "kuhimiza"); Balanced says "mahubiri" (preaching), as the English Balanced does; Readable uses the verb "tunapowahimiza". "Maonyo" would lean towards warning.

decisions.choice: nia chafu (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "uchafu" (impurity). In Balanced, "uchafu" alone could suggest sexual sin, while the charge here is impure motives (meaning decision), so Balanced says "nia chafu" (unclean motives), as the English Balanced says "impure motives".

source.text: οὔτε γάρ ποτε ἐν λόγῳ κολακείας ἐγενήθημεν, καθὼς οἴδατε, οὔτε ἐν προφάσει πλεονεξίας, θεὸς μάρτυς, οὔτε ζητοῦντες ἐξ ἀνθρώπων δόξαν, οὔτε ἀφ’ ὑμῶν οὔτε ἀπ’ ἄλλων, δυνάμενοι ἐν βάρει εἶναι ὡς Χριστοῦ ἀπόστολοι· ἀλλὰ ἐγενήθημεν ἤπιοι ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν, ὡς ἐὰν τροφὸς θάλπῃ τὰ ἑαυτῆς τέκνα·

records.literal_gloss: Neither for ever with word of flattery were we, as you know, nor with pretext of greed, God [is] witness, \v 6 nor seeking from men glory, neither from you nor from others, \v 7 being able to be in weight as Christ's apostles; but we became gentle in [the] midst of you, as if a nursing mother would cherish her own children;

en.L: For we never came with a word of flattery, as you know, nor with a pretext for greed (God [is] witness), \v 6 nor seeking glory from {{gender:people|men}}, neither from you nor from others, \v 7 though we could have been a weight [on you] as apostles of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}. But we were gentle among you, as a nursing mother cherishes her own children.
en.B: As you know, we never used flattery, and we never put on a show to cover up greed; God is our witness. \v 6 We did not look for praise from people, whether from you or from anyone else, \v 7 even though as apostles of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} we could have made our weight felt. Instead we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother who holds her own children close.
en.R: You know that we never tried to please you with nice words that were not true. We never pretended to care about you so that we could get money. God knows this is true. \v 6 We did not try to get people to praise us, not you or anyone else. \v 7 We are apostles of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so we could have made demands on you. But we were gentle with you, like a mother taking care of her own little children.

fr.L: Car jamais nous ne sommes venus avec une parole de flatterie, comme vous le savez, ni avec un prétexte pour la cupidité (Dieu [en est] témoin), \v 6 ni cherchant la gloire auprès des {{gender:humains|hommes}}, ni de vous ni d’autres, \v 7 alors que nous pouvions être un poids [pour vous] comme apôtres du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Mais nous avons été doux au milieu de vous, comme une mère qui allaite chérit ses propres enfants.
fr.B: Vous le savez, nous n’avons jamais usé de flatterie, et nous n’avons jamais joué la comédie pour masquer un désir de gain : Dieu en est témoin. \v 6 Nous n’avons pas cherché les éloges des gens, ni les vôtres ni ceux de personne d’autre, \v 7 alors qu’en tant qu’apôtres du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, nous aurions pu faire sentir notre poids. Au contraire, nous avons été doux parmi vous, comme une mère qui allaite et serre contre elle ses propres enfants.
fr.R: Vous savez que nous n’avons jamais essayé de vous plaire avec de belles paroles qui n’étaient pas vraies. Nous n’avons jamais fait semblant de nous intéresser à vous pour obtenir de l’argent. Dieu sait que c’est vrai. \v 6 Nous n’avons pas cherché à nous faire admirer par les gens, ni par vous ni par d’autres. \v 7 Nous sommes apôtres du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, alors nous aurions pu exiger beaucoup de vous. Mais nous avons été doux avec vous, comme une mère qui prend soin de ses tout-petits.

es.L: Porque nunca usamos palabras de adulación, como {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}}, ni pretexto para la avaricia (Dios [es] testigo), \v 6 ni buscando gloria de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}, ni de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ni de otros, \v 7 aunque podríamos haber sido una carga como apóstoles {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Al contrario, fuimos tiernos entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como una nodriza que cuida con cariño a sus propios hijos.
es.B: Como {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}}, nunca usamos la adulación ni fingimos para encubrir la avaricia; Dios es testigo. \v 6 No buscamos los elogios de la gente, ni de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ni de nadie, \v 7 aunque como apóstoles {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} podríamos haber hecho valer nuestro peso. Al contrario, fuimos tiernos entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como una madre que amamanta y abraza a sus propios hijos.
es.R: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que nunca tratamos de {{plural_you:agradarlos|agradaros}} con palabras bonitas que no eran verdad. Nunca fingimos que {{plural_you:nos importaban|nos importabais}} para sacar dinero. Dios sabe que esto es verdad. \v 6 No buscamos que la gente nos alabara, ni {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ni nadie más. \v 7 Somos apóstoles {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, así que podríamos haber{{plural_you:les|os}} exigido cosas. Pero fuimos tiernos con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como una madre que cuida a sus propios hijitos.

sw.L: Kwa maana hatukuwahi kuja na neno la kubembeleza, kama mjuavyo, wala kwa kisingizio cha tamaa ya mali (Mungu [ni] shahidi), \v 6 wala hatukutafuta utukufu kutoka kwa wanadamu, wala kutoka kwenu wala kutoka kwa wengine, \v 7 ingawa tungeweza kuwa mzigo [kwenu] kama mitume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Bali tulikuwa wapole kati yenu, kama mama anayenyonyesha anavyowatunza watoto wake mwenyewe.
sw.B: Kama mjuavyo, hatukuwahi kutumia maneno ya kubembeleza, wala hatukujifanya ili kuficha tamaa ya mali; Mungu ni shahidi wetu. \v 6 Hatukutafuta sifa kutoka kwa watu, iwe kwenu au kwa mtu mwingine yeyote, \v 7 ingawa kama mitume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} tungeweza kuonyesha uzito wa mamlaka yetu. Badala yake tulikuwa wapole kati yenu, kama mama anayenyonyesha anavyowakumbatia watoto wake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Mnajua kwamba hatukuwahi kujaribu kuwafurahisha kwa maneno matamu yasiyo ya kweli. Hatukuwahi kujifanya kuwajali ili tupate pesa kutoka kwenu. Mungu anajua kwamba hii ni kweli. \v 6 Hatukujaribu kuwafanya watu watusifu, ninyi wala mtu mwingine yeyote. \v 7 Sisi ni mitume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwa hiyo tungeweza kuwadai mambo mengi. Lakini tulikuwa wapole kwenu, kama mama anayewatunza watoto wake wadogo.

decisions.choice: flattery: the speaker's art of pleasing a crowd
decisions.reason: κολακείας is flattery used to win favor or money, a charge often laid against public speakers of the day.

decisions.choice: a pretext for greed: a show put on to hide a wish for gain
decisions.reason: προφάσει is a pretext or cover. Paul did not use preaching as a mask for making money (verse 9).

decisions.choice: God is witness: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: Paul calls God to witness what only God can see, his motives (Romans 1:9; Philippians 1:8).

decisions.choice: glory from people: praise and honor
decisions.reason: δόξαν here is the honor people give, not God's glory: Paul did not seek a reputation.

decisions.choice: be a weight: both make demands for support and assert authority
decisions.reason: βάρει means weight: a burden, or importance. As apostles they could have asked to be supported (verse 9 uses the related verb "burden") and could have stood on their dignity. Paul probably means both.

decisions.choice: apostles: messengers sent by Christ, here including Silvanus and Timothy
decisions.reason: The plural takes in the three senders of the letter. ἀπόστολοι can be used of messengers sent out by Christ beyond the Twelve (Romans 16:7).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "gentle"
decisions.reason: Many early manuscripts read "infants", a word that differs from ἤπιοι by one letter, and the word before it ends in that same letter, so a copyist could easily add it or drop it. "Gentle" fits the picture of the nursing mother; "infants" would be a sudden change of picture, though Paul does change pictures quickly (verses 11 and 17). Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: a nursing mother: a mother who nurses and warms her own children
decisions.reason: τροφὸς can be a nurse who cares for another's children, but "her own children" points to a mother. θάλπω means to keep warm, to cherish.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general; Balanced and Readable say "people".

decisions.choice: praise
decisions.reason: The sense here is honor from people (m4), so the key term "glory" is not used.

decisions.choice: nice words that were not true; pretended to care about you so that we could get money
alternatives: a word of flattery; a pretext for greed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what flattery and a pretext for greed are (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: une mère qui allaite
decisions.reason: The woman cherishes "her own" children (m8), so she is their mother; French "nourrice" today means a wet nurse or childminder caring for others' children.

decisions.choice: una carga (L); hacer valer nuestro peso (B); exigir cosas (R)
alternatives: ser una carga at every level
decisions.reason: The phrase means both asking for support and asserting authority (meaning decision). "Hacer valer nuestro peso" keeps the Greek picture of weight and both senses; Literal keeps the plain "carga".

decisions.choice: una nodriza (L); una madre que amamanta (B)
decisions.reason: The word is a nursing woman; she cares for "her own" children, so she is their mother. Literal keeps the word "nodriza"; Balanced says "madre que amamanta" so that readers do not picture a hired nurse.

decisions.choice: kuwa mzigo (L); kuonyesha uzito wa mamlaka yetu (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek "weight" means both making demands for support and asserting authority (meaning decision). Literal keeps the picture with "mzigo" (a burden); Balanced uses "uzito" (weight, importance), which in Swahili also means standing and authority; Readable says "kuwadai mambo mengi" (make many demands), as the English Readable does.

source.text: οὕτως ὁμειρόμενοι ὑμῶν εὐδοκοῦμεν μεταδοῦναι ὑμῖν οὐ μόνον τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ψυχάς, διότι ἀγαπητοὶ ἡμῖν ἐγενήθητε.

records.literal_gloss: So longing for you we were pleased to share with you not only the gospel of the God but also the our own lives, because beloved to us you became.

en.L: So, longing for you, we were pleased to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves, because you had become dear to us.
en.B: Our longing for you was such that we gladly gave you not only the gospel of God but ourselves too, for you had become dear to us.
en.R: We loved you so much that we were happy to tell you God's good news. But we also gave you our lives, because you had become very dear to us.

fr.L: Ainsi, éprouvant pour vous un vif attachement, nous avons trouvé bon de vous donner non seulement l’Évangile de Dieu, mais aussi nos propres vies, parce que vous nous étiez devenus chers.
fr.B: Notre attachement pour vous était tel que nous vous avons donné de bon cœur non seulement l’Évangile de Dieu, mais aussi notre propre vie, car vous nous étiez devenus chers.
fr.R: Nous vous aimions tellement que nous avons été heureux de vous annoncer la bonne nouvelle de Dieu. Et nous vous avons aussi donné notre vie, parce que vous nous étiez devenus très chers.

es.L: Así, sintiendo afecto por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, nos complacíamos en compartir con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no solo el evangelio de Dios, sino también nuestras propias vidas, porque {{plural_you:habían|habíais}} llegado a sernos queridos.
es.B: Tanto {{plural_you:los|os}} queríamos que con gusto {{plural_you:les|os}} dimos no solo el evangelio de Dios, sino también nuestras propias vidas, porque {{plural_you:habían|habíais}} llegado a ser muy queridos para nosotros.
es.R: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} queríamos tanto que nos alegraba anunciar{{plural_you:les|os}} la buena noticia de Dios. Pero también {{plural_you:les|os}} dimos nuestras vidas, porque {{plural_you:habían|habíais}} llegado a ser muy queridos para nosotros.

sw.L: Hivyo, tukiwaonea shauku, tulipendezwa kuwashirikisha si Injili ya Mungu tu, bali pia nafsi zetu wenyewe, kwa sababu mlikuwa wapendwa kwetu.
sw.B: Tuliwaonea shauku kiasi kwamba tulifurahi kuwapa si Injili ya Mungu tu, bali na nafsi zetu pia, kwa maana mlikuwa wapendwa sana kwetu.
sw.R: Tuliwapenda sana, hata tukafurahi kuwaeleza Habari Njema ya Mungu. Lakini pia tuliwapa maisha yetu, kwa sababu mlikuwa wapendwa sana kwetu.

decisions.choice: longing for you: deep affection
decisions.reason: ὁμειρόμενοι is a rare word for yearning, used on old tombstones of parents' longing for a lost child. It carries on the picture of the nursing mother (verse 7).

decisions.choice: our own selves: our lives
decisions.reason: ψυχάς is the self, the life. They shared their whole selves, not only a message.

decisions.choice: We loved you so much
decisions.reason: Readable puts the rare word in everyday words.

decisions.choice: nuestras propias vidas
decisions.reason: "Almas" would suggest only the inner self; the meaning decision reads the word as their lives, which "vidas" says plainly.

decisions.choice: nafsi zetu (L, B); maisha yetu (R)
decisions.reason: "Nafsi" is the self, the whole person, which is what Paul gave (meaning decision: our lives); "roho zetu" would be heard as "our spirits". Readable says "maisha yetu" (our lives).

source.text: Μνημονεύετε γάρ, ἀδελφοί, τὸν κόπον ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν μόχθον· νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐργαζόμενοι πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐπιβαρῆσαί τινα ὑμῶν ἐκηρύξαμεν εἰς ὑμᾶς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: You remember for, brothers, the labor of us and the toil; night and day working so as not to burden any of you we proclaimed to you the gospel of the God.

en.L: For you remember, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, our labor and toil: working night and day so as not to be a burden to any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
en.B: You remember, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, how hard we worked and toiled: we labored night and day so as not to be a burden to any of you while we preached the gospel of God to you.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, you remember how hard we worked. We worked day and night so that we would not have to ask any of you for money. And while we did that, we told you God's good news.

fr.L: Car vous vous souvenez, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, de notre labeur et de notre peine : travaillant nuit et jour pour n’être à charge à aucun de vous, nous vous avons proclamé l’Évangile de Dieu.
fr.B: Vous vous rappelez, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, combien nous avons travaillé et peiné : nous avons travaillé nuit et jour pour n’être à la charge d’aucun de vous, pendant que nous vous prêchions l’Évangile de Dieu.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, vous vous rappelez combien nous avons travaillé dur. Nous avons travaillé jour et nuit pour ne pas avoir à vous demander de l’argent. Et pendant ce temps, nous vous avons annoncé la bonne nouvelle de Dieu.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:se acuerdan|os acordáis}}, hermanos, de nuestro trabajo y fatiga: trabajando de noche y de día para no ser una carga a ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} proclamamos el evangelio de Dios.
es.B: {{plural_you:Recuerdan|Recordáis}}, hermanos, cuánto trabajamos y nos fatigamos: trabajábamos de noche y de día para no ser una carga a ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mientras {{plural_you:les|os}} predicábamos el evangelio de Dios.
es.R: Hermanos, {{plural_you:recuerdan|recordáis}} lo mucho que trabajamos. Trabajábamos día y noche para no tener que pedir dinero a ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Y mientras tanto, {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciábamos la buena noticia de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana mnakumbuka, ndugu, juhudi yetu na taabu: tukifanya kazi usiku na mchana ili tusimlemee yeyote kati yenu, tuliwahubiria Injili ya Mungu.
sw.B: Ndugu, mnakumbuka jinsi tulivyofanya kazi kwa juhudi na taabu: tulifanya kazi usiku na mchana ili tusimlemee yeyote kati yenu, huku tukiwahubiria Injili ya Mungu.
sw.R: Ndugu, mnakumbuka jinsi tulivyofanya kazi kwa bidii. Tulifanya kazi mchana na usiku ili tusilazimike kumwomba yeyote kati yenu pesa. Na wakati huo huo tuliwaeleza Habari Njema ya Mungu.

decisions.choice: working night and day: Paul supported himself by his trade
decisions.reason: Paul worked with his hands, making tents or leather goods (Acts 18:3), so that no one could say he preached for money. He did accept gifts from Philippi while in Thessalonica (Philippians 4:16).

decisions.choice: night and day: all the time
decisions.reason: The order follows the Jewish day, which began at sunset. It means constantly, from before dawn into the night.

decisions.choice: burden: be a cost to them
decisions.reason: ἐπιβαρέω means to weigh down, here by needing to be supported (compare verse 7).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: so that we would not have to ask any of you for money
alternatives: so as not to burden any of you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the burden would have been (m3).

decisions.choice: juhudi na taabu
decisions.reason: "Juhudi" (hard effort) for the word rendered so in 1:3, and "taabu" (toil, hardship) for the second word, so that the pair stays two words in Swahili as in the Greek.

source.text: ὑμεῖς μάρτυρες καὶ ὁ θεός, ὡς ὁσίως καὶ δικαίως καὶ ἀμέμπτως ὑμῖν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐγενήθημεν, καθάπερ οἴδατε ὡς ἕνα ἕκαστον ὑμῶν ὡς πατὴρ τέκνα ἑαυτοῦ παρακαλοῦντες ὑμᾶς καὶ παραμυθούμενοι καὶ μαρτυρόμενοι, εἰς τὸ περιπατεῖν ὑμᾶς ἀξίως τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ καλοῦντος ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ βασιλείαν καὶ δόξαν.

records.literal_gloss: You [are] witnesses and the God, how devoutly and justly and blamelessly to you the believing [ones] we were, \v 11 just as you know how each one of you as a father [his] children of himself, \v 12 exhorting you and encouraging and charging, unto the to walk you worthily of the God, the [one] calling you into the of himself kingdom and glory.

en.L: You [are] witnesses, and God [also], how devoutly and justly and blamelessly we behaved toward you who believe, \v 11 just as you know how, like a father with his own children, [we dealt with] each one of you, \v 12 exhorting you and encouraging [you] and urging [you] to walk worthily of God, who calls you into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own kingdom and glory.
en.B: God is our witness, and so are you: we lived among you believers in a way that was devout, just and without fault. \v 11 You know how we treated each one of you as a father treats his own children. \v 12 We urged you on, we comforted you, and we pleaded with you to live in a way that is worthy of God, who is calling you into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own kingdom and glory.
en.R: You saw how we lived among you who believe, and God saw it too. We were holy and did what was right, and no one could blame us for anything. \v 11 You know that we treated each of you the way a father treats his own children. \v 12 We encouraged you, comforted you and told you how important it is to live the way God wants. God is calling you into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom, to share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

fr.L: Vous [êtes] témoins, et Dieu [aussi], de la manière sainte et juste et irréprochable dont nous nous sommes conduits envers vous qui croyez, \v 11 de même que vous savez comment, comme un père avec ses propres enfants, [nous avons agi avec] chacun de vous, \v 12 vous exhortant et [vous] encourageant et [vous] adjurant de marcher d’une manière digne de Dieu, qui vous appelle à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre royaume et à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire.
fr.B: Dieu en est témoin, et vous aussi : nous avons vécu parmi vous, les croyants, d’une manière sainte, juste et irréprochable. \v 11 Vous savez que nous avons traité chacun de vous comme un père traite ses propres enfants. \v 12 Nous vous avons encouragés, nous vous avons réconfortés, et nous vous avons suppliés de vivre d’une manière digne de Dieu, qui vous appelle à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume et à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire.
fr.R: Vous avez vu comment nous avons vécu parmi vous qui croyez, et Dieu l’a vu aussi. Notre vie a été sainte, nous avons fait ce qui est juste, et personne n’a pu nous reprocher quoi que ce soit. \v 11 Vous savez que nous avons traité chacun de vous comme un père traite ses propres enfants. \v 12 Nous vous avons encouragés et réconfortés, et nous vous avons dit combien il est important de vivre comme Dieu le veut. Dieu vous appelle dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume, pour avoir part à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire.

es.L: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [son] testigos, y Dios [también], de cuán santa, justa e irreprochablemente nos comportamos con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que creen, \v 11 así como {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} cómo, como un padre con sus propios hijos, [tratamos] a cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \v 12 exhortándo{{plural_you:los|os}} y animándo{{plural_you:los|os}} y encargándo{{plural_you:les|os}} que {{plural_you:anduvieran|anduvierais}} como es digno de Dios, que {{plural_you:los|os}} llama a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio reino y gloria.
es.B: Dios es testigo, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también, de que vivimos entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los creyentes, de una manera santa, justa e irreprochable. \v 11 {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que tratamos a cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como un padre trata a sus propios hijos. \v 12 {{plural_you:Los|Os}} exhortamos, {{plural_you:los|os}} consolamos y {{plural_you:les|os}} rogamos encarecidamente que {{plural_you:vivieran|vivierais}} de una manera digna de Dios, que {{plural_you:los|os}} está llamando a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio reino y gloria.
es.R: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} cómo vivimos entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que creen, y Dios también lo vio. Fuimos santos e hicimos lo correcto, y nadie pudo acusarnos de nada. \v 11 {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que tratamos a cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como un padre trata a sus propios hijos. \v 12 {{plural_you:Los|Os}} animamos, {{plural_you:los|os}} consolamos y {{plural_you:les|os}} dijimos lo importante que es vivir como Dios quiere. Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} está llamando a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reino, para que {{plural_you:compartan|compartáis}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria.

sw.L: Ninyi [ni] mashahidi, na Mungu [pia], jinsi tulivyoishi kwa utakatifu na kwa haki na bila lawama kwenu ninyi mnaoamini, \v 11 kama mjuavyo jinsi, kama baba kwa watoto wake mwenyewe, [tulivyomtendea] kila mmoja wenu, \v 12 tukiwahimiza na kuwafariji na kuwasihi sana mwenende kwa namna inayomstahili Mungu, anayewaita katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe na utukufu.
sw.B: Mungu ni shahidi wetu, nanyi pia ni mashahidi: tuliishi kati yenu ninyi mnaoamini kwa utakatifu, kwa haki na bila lawama. \v 11 Mnajua jinsi tulivyomtendea kila mmoja wenu kama baba anavyowatendea watoto wake mwenyewe. \v 12 Tuliwahimiza, tukawafariji, na kuwasihi sana mwishi maisha yanayomstahili Mungu, anayewaita katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe na utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Mliona jinsi tulivyoishi kati yenu ninyi mnaoamini, na Mungu aliona pia. Tulikuwa watakatifu, tulifanya yaliyo haki, na hakuna mtu ambaye angeweza kutulaumu kwa jambo lolote. \v 11 Mnajua kwamba tulimtendea kila mmoja wenu kama baba anavyowatendea watoto wake mwenyewe. \v 12 Tuliwatia moyo, tukawafariji, na kuwaambia jinsi ilivyo muhimu kuishi kama Mungu anavyotaka. Mungu anawaita katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, ili mshiriki utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: devoutly, justly, blamelessly: right before God, right toward people, and open to no charge
decisions.reason: ὁσίως is holiness toward God, δικαίως uprightness toward others, and ἀμέμπτως means that no one could fairly accuse them.

decisions.choice: the sentence has no main verb: "we dealt with" each of you is understood
decisions.reason: Paul begins "how each one of you, as a father his own children", and goes straight to the participles of verse 12. The verb is left to be understood.

decisions.choice: urging, comforting, solemnly charging
decisions.reason: παρακαλοῦντες is to urge or appeal, παραμυθούμενοι to comfort or console, μαρτυρόμενοι to insist solemnly. A father does all three.

decisions.choice: who calls you into his kingdom and glory: God's call goes on, toward the kingdom still to come
decisions.reason: The present καλοῦντος says God is still calling. His kingdom and glory are what believers will share at Christ's coming (Romans 5:2).

decisions.choice: [we dealt with]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb to be understood (m2).

decisions.choice: live
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure for how one lives; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: to share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory
decisions.reason: Readable says how they are called into God's glory (m4).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire
decisions.reason: The Greek has one "his own" for both nouns; French repeats the possessive, which agrees with each noun, so each carries its own span.

decisions.choice: exhortándo{{plural_you:los|os}} ... encargándo{{plural_you:les|os}}
decisions.reason: Spanish joins the object pronoun to the gerund; the plural_you span covers only the ending, so the vosotros form reads "exhortándoos".

decisions.choice: que anduvieran
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of walking for the way one lives; Balanced and Readable say "vivir".

decisions.choice: mwenende (L); mwishi maisha (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Paul's picture of walking with "kuenenda", the Swahili word for walking that is also used of conduct; Balanced says "kuishi maisha" (live a life), as the English Balanced says "live". "Kutembea" would sound like a stroll.

source.text: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡμεῖς εὐχαριστοῦμεν τῷ θεῷ ἀδιαλείπτως, ὅτι παραλαβόντες λόγον ἀκοῆς παρ’ ἡμῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐδέξασθε οὐ λόγον ἀνθρώπων ἀλλὰ καθὼς ἀληθῶς ἐστὶν λόγον θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἐνεργεῖται ἐν ὑμῖν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And because of this also we give thanks to the God unceasingly, that having received [the] word of hearing from us of the God you accepted [it] not [as the] word of men but just as it truly is, [the] word of God, which also is at work in you the believing [ones].

en.L: And because of this we also thank God unceasingly, that when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you accepted [it] not [as] the word of {{gender:people|men}} but as what it truly is, the word of God, which is also at work in you who believe.
en.B: And we too give thanks to God without ceasing for this: when you received from us the word of God that you heard, you welcomed it not as a human message but as what it really is, God's own word, which is now at work in you who believe.
en.R: We never stop thanking God for this: when we told you God's message, you did not think of it as something people made up. You accepted it as what it really is, the message from God. And that message is working in you who believe.

fr.L: Et c’est pourquoi nous aussi, nous rendons grâce à Dieu sans cesse de ce que, ayant reçu de nous la parole de Dieu que vous avez entendue, vous [l’]avez accueillie non [comme] parole d’{{gender:humains|hommes}}, mais comme ce qu’elle est vraiment, la parole de Dieu, qui agit aussi en vous qui croyez.
fr.B: Et nous aussi, nous rendons grâce à Dieu sans cesse pour ceci : quand vous avez reçu de nous la parole de Dieu que vous avez entendue, vous l’avez accueillie non comme un message humain, mais comme ce qu’elle est réellement, la parole même de Dieu, qui agit maintenant en vous qui croyez.
fr.R: Nous ne cessons pas de remercier Dieu pour ceci : quand nous vous avons annoncé le message de Dieu, vous n’avez pas pensé que c’était une invention humaine. Vous l’avez accepté pour ce qu’il est vraiment : le message qui vient de Dieu. Et ce message agit en vous qui croyez.

es.L: Y por esto también nosotros damos gracias a Dios sin cesar, de que, al recibir la palabra de Dios que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} de nosotros, la {{plural_you:acogieron|acogisteis}} no [como] palabra de {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}, sino como lo que verdaderamente es, palabra de Dios, la cual también actúa en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que creen.
es.B: Por eso también nosotros damos gracias a Dios sin cesar: cuando {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} la palabra de Dios que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} de nosotros, no la {{plural_you:acogieron|acogisteis}} como un mensaje humano, sino como lo que realmente es, la palabra de Dios, que ahora actúa en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que creen.
es.R: Nunca dejamos de dar gracias a Dios por esto: cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos el mensaje de Dios, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no {{plural_you:pensaron|pensasteis}} que era algo inventado por la gente. Lo {{plural_you:aceptaron|aceptasteis}} como lo que realmente es, el mensaje de Dios. Y ese mensaje está obrando en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que creen.

sw.L: Na kwa sababu hii sisi pia tunamshukuru Mungu bila kukoma, kwamba mlipolipokea neno la Mungu mlilolisikia kutoka kwetu, mlilikubali si [kama] neno la wanadamu, bali kama lilivyo kweli, neno la Mungu, ambalo pia linatenda kazi ndani yenu ninyi mnaoamini.
sw.B: Nasi pia tunamshukuru Mungu bila kukoma kwa jambo hili: mlipolipokea kutoka kwetu neno la Mungu mlilolisikia, hamkulikaribisha kama ujumbe wa kibinadamu, bali kama lilivyo kweli, neno la Mungu mwenyewe, ambalo sasa linafanya kazi ndani yenu ninyi mnaoamini.
sw.R: Hatuachi kumshukuru Mungu kwa jambo hili: tulipowaeleza ujumbe wa Mungu, hamkuuona kama kitu ambacho watu wamebuni. Mliupokea kama ulivyo kweli, ujumbe kutoka kwa Mungu. Na ujumbe huo unafanya kazi ndani yenu ninyi mnaoamini.

decisions.choice: because of this: for what follows, the way they received the word
decisions.reason: διὰ τοῦτο most naturally points ahead to the reason Paul gives in the same sentence.

decisions.choice: received, then welcomed
decisions.reason: παραλαμβάνω is the word for receiving what is handed on (Colossians 2:6); δέχομαι is to welcome, to accept gladly. They heard the message and took it to heart.

decisions.choice: the word of hearing from us, of God: the message they heard from Paul, which is God's
decisions.reason: The phrase piles up genitives: the word they heard, which came from Paul and his companions, and which belongs to God.

decisions.choice: which is at work: the word itself works in them
decisions.reason: ὃς most naturally refers to "word". ἐνεργέω in the middle voice means to be at work by its own power (Colossians 1:29).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general; Balanced says "human" and Readable "people".

decisions.choice: recibir ... acoger
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two verbs: one for receiving what is handed on, one for welcoming it (meaning decision). "Recibir" and "acoger" keep the difference.

decisions.choice: mlipolipokea ... mlilikubali (L); mlipolipokea ... hamkulikaribisha (B)
decisions.reason: Paul uses two verbs: they received the word, then welcomed it (meaning decision). Swahili keeps them apart with "kupokea" for the first and "kukubali" (Literal) or "kukaribisha" (Balanced, to welcome a guest) for the second.

source.text: ὑμεῖς γὰρ μιμηταὶ ἐγενήθητε, ἀδελφοί, τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ τῶν οὐσῶν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι τὰ αὐτὰ ἐπάθετε καὶ ὑμεῖς ὑπὸ τῶν ἰδίων συμφυλετῶν καθὼς καὶ αὐτοὶ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων τῶν καὶ τὸν κύριον ἀποκτεινάντων Ἰησοῦν καὶ τοὺς προφήτας καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐκδιωξάντων, καὶ θεῷ μὴ ἀρεσκόντων, καὶ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ἐναντίων, κωλυόντων ἡμᾶς τοῖς ἔθνεσιν λαλῆσαι ἵνα σωθῶσιν, εἰς τὸ ἀναπληρῶσαι αὐτῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας πάντοτε.

records.literal_gloss: You for imitators became, brothers, of the churches of the God being in the Judea in Christ Jesus, because the same things suffered also you from the own countrymen as also they from the Jews, \v 15 the [ones] both the Lord having killed, Jesus, and the prophets, and us having driven out, and God not pleasing, and to all men hostile, \v 16 hindering us to the Gentiles to speak so that they may be saved, so as to fill up their sins always.

en.L: For you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, became imitators of the churches of God that are in Judea in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, because you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews, \v 15 who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out, and do not please God, and are hostile to all {{gender:people|men}}, \v 16 hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they may be saved, so as always to fill up their sins.
en.B: For you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, followed the example of God's churches in Judea that are in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. You suffered from your own people the same things they suffered from the Jews of Judea, \v 15 who killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets and drove us out. They do not please God and they are hostile to everyone, \v 16 because they try to stop us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they may be saved. In this way they keep filling up the full measure of their sins.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, the same thing happened to you that happened to God's churches in Judea, who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. Your own people made you suffer, just as those Jews in Judea who were against the believers made them suffer. \v 15 They killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and they forced us to leave. They do not please God, and they are against everyone. \v 16 They try to stop us from telling people who are not Jews how to be saved. So they keep adding more and more to their sins.

fr.L: Car vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, vous êtes devenus imitateurs des églises de Dieu qui sont en Judée {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, parce que vous aussi, vous avez souffert de la part de vos propres compatriotes les mêmes choses qu’eux de la part des Juifs, \v 15 qui ont tué et le Seigneur Jésus et les prophètes, et nous ont chassés, et ne plaisent pas à Dieu, et sont hostiles à tous les {{gender:humains|hommes}}, \v 16 nous empêchant de parler aux nations pour qu’elles soient sauvées, de manière à mettre toujours le comble à leurs péchés.
fr.B: Car vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, vous avez suivi l’exemple des églises de Dieu qui sont en Judée {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus. Vous avez souffert de la part de vos propres compatriotes ce qu’elles ont souffert de la part des Juifs de Judée, \v 15 qui ont tué le Seigneur Jésus et les prophètes, et qui nous ont chassés. Ils ne plaisent pas à Dieu et sont hostiles à tout le monde, \v 16 puisqu’ils essaient de nous empêcher de parler aux non-Juifs pour qu’ils soient sauvés. Ainsi, ils ne cessent de mettre le comble à leurs péchés.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, il vous est arrivé la même chose qu’aux églises de Dieu en Judée, qui appartiennent au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. Les gens de votre propre ville vous ont fait souffrir, comme ces Juifs de Judée qui s’opposaient aux croyants ont fait souffrir les églises de là-bas. \v 15 Ils ont tué le Seigneur Jésus et les prophètes, et ils nous ont obligés à partir. Ils ne plaisent pas à Dieu, et ils sont contre tout le monde. \v 16 Ils essaient de nous empêcher de dire aux gens qui ne sont pas juifs comment être sauvés. Ainsi, ils ajoutent sans cesse de nouveaux péchés à leurs péchés.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos, {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a ser imitadores de las iglesias de Dios que están en Judea en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, porque también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:padecieron|padecisteis}} las mismas cosas de parte de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios compatriotas, como ellos de parte de los judíos, \v 15 los cuales mataron tanto al Señor Jesús como a los profetas, y nos expulsaron a nosotros, y no agradan a Dios, y son hostiles a todos {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}, \v 16 impidiéndonos hablar a los gentiles para que sean salvos, de modo que siempre colman [la medida de] sus pecados.
es.B: Porque {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos, {{plural_you:siguieron|seguisteis}} el ejemplo de las iglesias de Dios en Judea que están en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}. De {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios compatriotas {{plural_you:sufrieron|sufristeis}} lo mismo que ellas sufrieron de los judíos de Judea, \v 15 que mataron al Señor Jesús y a los profetas, y nos expulsaron a nosotros. No agradan a Dios y son hostiles a todos, \v 16 porque intentan impedirnos hablar a los gentiles para que se salven. Así siguen colmando la medida de sus pecados.
es.R: Hermanos, a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:les|os}} pasó lo mismo que a las iglesias de Dios en Judea, que pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}. La gente de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} propia ciudad {{plural_you:los|os}} hizo sufrir, igual que aquellos judíos de Judea que estaban en contra de los creyentes los hicieron sufrir a ellos. \v 15 Ellos mataron al Señor Jesús y a los profetas, y a nosotros nos obligaron a irnos. No agradan a Dios y están en contra de todos. \v 16 Intentan impedir que les digamos a los que no son judíos cómo pueden salvarse. Así siguen añadiendo más y más a sus pecados.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninyi, ndugu, mlikuwa waigaji wa makanisa ya Mungu yaliyoko Uyahudi katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, kwa sababu ninyi pia mliteswa mambo yale yale na wananchi wenzenu wenyewe kama wao walivyoteswa na Wayahudi, \v 15 ambao walimuua Bwana Yesu na manabii, na wakatufukuza sisi, wala hawampendezi Mungu, na ni maadui wa watu wote, \v 16 wakituzuia tusiseme na watu wa mataifa ili waokolewe, hata kujaza dhambi zao siku zote.
sw.B: Kwa maana ninyi, ndugu, mlifuata mfano wa makanisa ya Mungu yaliyoko Uyahudi, yaliyo katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Mliteswa na wananchi wenzenu mambo yale yale ambayo wao waliteswa na Wayahudi wa Uyahudi, \v 15 waliomuua Bwana Yesu na manabii, wakatufukuza sisi pia. Hawampendezi Mungu, na ni maadui wa watu wote, \v 16 kwa sababu wanajaribu kutuzuia tusiseme na watu wa mataifa ili waokolewe. Kwa njia hiyo wanaendelea kujaza kipimo kamili cha dhambi zao.
sw.R: Ndugu, yaliyowapata ninyi ndiyo yaliyoyapata makanisa ya Mungu huko Uyahudi, yaliyo ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Watu wa mji wenu wenyewe waliwatesa, kama vile wale Wayahudi wa Uyahudi waliowapinga waamini walivyoyatesa makanisa hayo. \v 15 Wao walimuua Bwana Yesu na manabii, wakatulazimisha kuondoka. Hawampendezi Mungu, na wanampinga kila mtu. \v 16 Wanajaribu kutuzuia tusiwaeleze watu wasio Wayahudi jinsi ya kuokolewa. Kwa hiyo wanaendelea kuongeza dhambi zao zaidi na zaidi.

decisions.choice: the churches of God in Judea: the first churches, of Jewish believers
decisions.reason: The churches of Judea were made up of Jews who believed in Jesus. They were persecuted from early on (Acts 8:1; Galatians 1:22-23).

decisions.choice: your own countrymen: fellow citizens of Thessalonica
decisions.reason: The Thessalonian believers suffered at the hands of their own townspeople, who were stirred up against them (Acts 17:5-9).

decisions.choice: the Jews here: those in Judea who persecuted the churches there, not the Jewish people as a whole
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: Ἰουδαίων can mean "the Jews" or "the Judeans", and the setting is Judea. The phrase is parallel to "your own countrymen": not every Thessalonian persecuted the church, and not every Jew did. Paul himself was a Jew, as were the Judean churches he praises in the same sentence, and in Romans 9:1-5 and 11:1-2, 11:25-29 he speaks of his own people with grief and hope. The words describe the opponents who killed the prophets, opposed Jesus and drove Paul out; they cannot be used against Jewish people as such.

decisions.choice: who killed the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus was executed by the Roman governor at the urging of leaders in Jerusalem (Mark 15:1-15). Acts 4:27 names Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel together as having opposed him.

decisions.choice: and the prophets: the prophets God sent to Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus spoke of those who killed the prophets (Matthew 23:31, 23:37), as Elijah had (1 Kings 19:10). Many later manuscripts read "their own prophets".

decisions.choice: drove us out: from Thessalonica, and then from Berea
decisions.reason: Acts 17:5-10 and 17:13 tell how opponents forced Paul to leave Thessalonica and then followed him to Berea.

decisions.choice: hostile to all people: shown by stopping the gospel from reaching the Gentiles
decisions.reason: Verse 16 explains the hostility: they try to keep the message of salvation from the nations.

decisions.choice: to fill up their sins: to fill the measure of sin
decisions.reason: In Genesis 15:16 the wrong of the Amorites is "not yet complete"; Jesus says "fill up the measure of your fathers" (Matthew 23:32). The picture is of a measure filled to the brim, after which judgment comes (verse 16).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: the Jews of Judea (B); those Jews in Judea who were against the believers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m3, which is uncertain: Literal keeps "the Jews".

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles".

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); les gens qui ne sont pas juifs (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms: "les nations" keeps the biblical sense of the peoples other than Israel; Balanced and Readable say plainly who they are, as the English "Gentiles" and "people who are not Jews" do.

decisions.choice: mettre le comble à leurs péchés
alternatives: remplir la mesure de leurs péchés
decisions.reason: The image is of a measure of sin filled to the top (m8); French "mettre le comble à" is the idiom for it, while "combler" alone would read as "make up for".

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los judíos de Judea (B); aquellos judíos de Judea que estaban en contra de los creyentes (R)
decisions.reason: As in the English, Balanced and Readable make explicit that Paul means those in Judea who persecuted the churches there, not the Jewish people as a whole (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: colmar [la medida de] sus pecados
decisions.reason: "Colmar la medida" is the Spanish idiom for filling a measure to the brim, which is the picture the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: wananchi wenzenu
decisions.reason: The countrymen are fellow citizens of Thessalonica (meaning decision), not a nation, so Swahili says "wananchi wenzenu" (your fellow citizens), and Readable "watu wa mji wenu" (the people of your city).

decisions.choice: Wayahudi (L); Wayahudi wa Uyahudi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Balanced and Readable say that the persecutors meant here are the Jews of Judea who opposed the churches there, not the Jewish people as a whole (meaning decision). Judea is "Uyahudi", as in John and Acts.

source.text: ἔφθασεν δὲ ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἡ ὀργὴ εἰς τέλος.

records.literal_gloss: Has come but upon them the wrath to [the] end.

en.L: But the wrath has come upon them to the end.
en.B: But the wrath has come upon them at last.
en.R: But God's anger has finally come upon them.

fr.L: Mais la colère est venue sur eux jusqu’à la fin.
fr.B: Mais la colère les a enfin atteints.
fr.R: Mais la colère de Dieu les a finalement atteints.

es.L: Pero la ira ha llegado sobre ellos hasta el fin.
es.B: Pero la ira ha caído por fin sobre ellos.
es.R: Pero por fin la ira de Dios ha caído sobre ellos.

sw.R: Lakini mwishowe ghadhabu ya Mungu imewajia.

decisions.choice: the wrath has come upon them at last: God's judgment, sure and final
decisions.reason: εἰς τέλος can mean "at last", "completely" or "until the end". The past tense may speak of judgment as already certain, or of some event Paul had in mind; the letter does not say which. "The wrath" is God's judgment, as in 1:10 and 5:9.

decisions.choice: God's anger
decisions.reason: Readable says whose wrath it is (as in 1:10).

source.text: Ἡμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἀπορφανισθέντες ἀφ’ ὑμῶν πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας, προσώπῳ οὐ καρδίᾳ, περισσοτέρως ἐσπουδάσαμεν τὸ πρόσωπον ὑμῶν ἰδεῖν ἐν πολλῇ ἐπιθυμίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: We but, brothers, having been orphaned from you for a time of an hour, in face not in heart, more abundantly were eager the face of you to see with much desire.

en.L: But we, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, having been orphaned from you for a short time, in face not in heart, were all the more eager to see your face, with great desire.
en.B: But we, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, were torn away from you for a short time, in person though not in heart, and we longed all the more eagerly to see you face to face.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we had to leave you for a short time. We were not with you in person, but we were still with you in our hearts. We wanted very much to see you again, and we tried hard to come back.

fr.L: Mais nous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, ayant été rendus orphelins de vous pour le temps d’une heure, de visage, non de cœur, nous nous sommes d’autant plus empressés de voir votre visage, avec un grand désir.
fr.B: Quant à nous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, arrachés à vous pour un peu de temps, loin des yeux mais non du cœur, nous avons désiré d’autant plus ardemment vous revoir face à face.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, nous avons dû vous quitter pour un peu de temps. Nous n’étions plus avec vous en personne, mais nous restions avec vous dans notre cœur. Nous voulions beaucoup vous revoir, et nous avons fait de gros efforts pour revenir.

es.L: Pero nosotros, hermanos, habiendo quedado huérfanos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por un corto tiempo, en presencia, no en el corazón, procuramos con mayor empeño ver {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} rostro, con mucho deseo.
es.B: Pero nosotros, hermanos, al ser arrancados de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por un corto tiempo, lejos en persona aunque no en el corazón, deseamos con mayor empeño {{plural_you:verlos|veros}} cara a cara.
es.R: Hermanos, tuvimos que {{plural_you:dejarlos|dejaros}} por un tiempo corto. No estábamos con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en persona, pero sí en el corazón. Deseábamos mucho volver a {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}, e hicimos todo lo posible por regresar.

sw.L: Lakini sisi, ndugu, tukiwa tumefanywa yatima kwa kutengwa nanyi kwa muda mfupi, kwa uso si kwa moyo, tulitamani zaidi sana kuuona uso wenu, kwa shauku kubwa.
sw.B: Lakini sisi, ndugu, tulipokonywa kutoka kwenu kwa muda mfupi, kwa mwili ingawa si kwa moyo, nasi tukatamani zaidi sana kuwaona ana kwa ana.
sw.R: Ndugu, tulilazimika kuwaacha kwa muda mfupi. Hatukuwa pamoja nanyi kimwili, lakini mioyo yetu ilikuwa bado pamoja nanyi. Tulitamani sana kuwaona tena, tukajitahidi sana kurudi.

decisions.choice: orphaned: bereaved, torn away
decisions.reason: ἀπορφανίζω means to be made an orphan, or bereaved. After picturing himself as mother (verse 7) and father (verse 11), Paul now feels like a child torn from its parents.

decisions.choice: for a time of an hour: a short while
decisions.reason: A way of saying a brief time.

decisions.choice: in face, not in heart: absent in person, present in heart
decisions.reason: Compare Colossians 2:5.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: torn away
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the pain of the word in plainer English (m1).

decisions.choice: loin des yeux mais non du cœur
alternatives: absents de corps mais non de cœur
decisions.reason: Paul's "in face, not in heart" (m3) turns the French proverb "loin des yeux, loin du cœur" on its head, which says the same thing in familiar words.

decisions.choice: quedar huérfanos (L); ser arrancados (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is "orphaned": the pain of a child torn from parents. Literal keeps "huérfanos"; Balanced says "arrancados", as the English says "torn away".

decisions.choice: tumefanywa yatima (L); tulipokonywa (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Paul's picture of being orphaned with "kufanywa yatima"; Balanced says "kupokonywa" (to be snatched away), as the English Balanced says "torn away". "Kutengwa" (to be separated) alone would lose the grief in the word.

source.text: διότι ἠθελήσαμεν ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐγὼ μὲν Παῦλος καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς, καὶ ἐνέκοψεν ἡμᾶς ὁ Σατανᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Because we wanted to come to you, I indeed Paul both once and twice, and hindered us the Satan.

en.L: For we wanted to come to you, I, Paul, both once and twice, and Satan hindered us.
en.B: We did want to come to you, and I, Paul, tried more than once, but Satan stood in our way.
en.R: We wanted to visit you. I, Paul, tried more than once, but Satan stopped us.

fr.L: Car nous avons voulu venir vers vous, moi Paul, et une fois et deux fois, et Satan nous [en] a empêchés.
fr.B: Nous avons vraiment voulu venir chez vous, et moi, Paul, j’ai essayé plus d’une fois, mais Satan nous a barré la route.
fr.R: Nous voulions vous rendre visite. Moi, Paul, j’ai essayé plusieurs fois, mais Satan nous en a empêchés.

es.L: Porque quisimos ir a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, yo, Pablo, una y otra vez, y Satanás nos lo impidió.
es.B: Sí, quisimos ir a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y yo, Pablo, lo intenté más de una vez, pero Satanás nos cerró el paso.
es.R: Queríamos {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}}. Yo, Pablo, lo intenté más de una vez, pero Satanás nos lo impidió.

sw.L: Kwa sababu tulitaka kuja kwenu, mimi Paulo hasa, mara moja na mara mbili, na Shetani akatuzuia.
sw.B: Tulitaka kweli kuja kwenu, nami Paulo nilijaribu zaidi ya mara moja, lakini Shetani alituwekea kizuizi.
sw.R: Tulitaka kuja kuwatembelea. Mimi Paulo nilijaribu zaidi ya mara moja, lakini Shetani alituzuia.

decisions.choice: once and twice: more than once
decisions.reason: A Greek way of saying "again and again" (Philippians 4:16).

decisions.choice: hindered: cut in, blocked the way
decisions.reason: ἐγκόπτω was used of cutting up a road to stop an advance.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary of God's people
decisions.reason: Paul does not say how Satan hindered him; he sees a spiritual enemy behind the obstacles (compare 3:5).

decisions.choice: una y otra vez
decisions.reason: The Greek "once and twice" is an idiom for more than once (meaning decision); Spanish "una y otra vez" is the matching idiom.

source.text: τίς γὰρ ἡμῶν ἐλπὶς ἢ χαρὰ ἢ στέφανος καυχήσεως ἢ οὐχὶ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ παρουσίᾳ;

records.literal_gloss: What for [is] our hope or joy or crown of boasting, or [is it] not even you, before the Lord of us Jesus at the of him coming?

en.L: For what [is] our hope or joy or crown of boasting before our Lord Jesus at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming? Is it not you also?
en.B: When our Lord Jesus comes, what will be our hope and joy, the crown we will be proud of before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? Surely it will be you, too.
en.R: When our Lord Jesus comes back, we will stand before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. What will give us hope and joy then? What will we be proud of, like a winner's crown? It will be you!

fr.L: Car quelle [est] notre espérance, ou joie, ou couronne de fierté devant notre Seigneur Jésus lors de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} venue ? N’est-ce pas vous aussi ?
fr.B: Quand notre Seigneur Jésus viendra, quelle sera notre espérance, notre joie, la couronne dont nous serons fiers devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ? C’est bien vous, vous aussi.
fr.R: Quand notre Seigneur Jésus reviendra, nous serons devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Qu’est-ce qui nous donnera alors de l’espérance et de la joie ? De quoi serons-nous fiers, comme d’une couronne de vainqueur ? Ce sera vous !

es.L: Porque ¿cuál [es] nuestra esperanza o gozo o corona de orgullo delante de nuestro Señor Jesús en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} venida? ¿No [lo son] también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: Cuando venga nuestro Señor Jesús, ¿cuál será nuestra esperanza y nuestra alegría, la corona de la que nos sentiremos orgullosos delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}? ¡Sin duda {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}!
es.R: Cuando nuestro Señor Jesús vuelva, estaremos delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. ¿Qué nos dará entonces esperanza y alegría? ¿De qué estaremos orgullosos, como de la corona de un ganador? ¡De {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}!

sw.L: Kwa maana tumaini letu au furaha au taji ya fahari [ni nini] mbele ya Bwana wetu Yesu wakati wa kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}? Je, si ninyi pia?
sw.B: Bwana wetu Yesu atakapokuja, tumaini letu na furaha yetu, taji tutakayoionea fahari mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, vitakuwa nini? Hakika mtakuwa ninyi pia.
sw.R: Bwana wetu Yesu atakaporudi, tutasimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Wakati huo ni nini kitakachotupa tumaini na furaha? Ni nini tutakachokionea fahari, kama taji ya mshindi? Ni ninyi!

decisions.choice: crown of boasting: a victor's wreath, the reward of work well done
decisions.reason: στέφανος is the wreath given to a winner in the games or worn at a festival. καυχήσεως is not empty pride but rightful joy in what God has done through one's work (Philippians 2:16; 4:1).

decisions.choice: coming: Christ's arrival
decisions.reason: παρουσίᾳ means presence or arrival, and was used for the official visit of a ruler to a city. In this letter it is Christ's coming (3:13; 4:15; 5:23).

decisions.choice: is it not you also: you, as well as the other churches
decisions.reason: καὶ ("also") hints that other churches will be Paul's joy too.

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable start from Christ's coming
decisions.reason: The Greek holds the time to the end; English reads more easily with it first.

decisions.choice: like a winner's crown
decisions.reason: Readable explains the crown (m1).

decisions.choice: venida (L); cuando venga (B); cuando vuelva (R)
decisions.reason: The word for Christ's arrival is "venida", the project's term for this word in the letters; Balanced and Readable turn it into a verb, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kuja kwake (L); atakapokuja (B); atakaporudi (R)
decisions.reason: Recorded once for both letters. Paul's word for Christ's coming is an arrival (meaning decision), so Literal keeps the noun "kuja" (the coming), as James 5:7-8 does, and Balanced turns it into the verb "atakapokuja". Readable says "atakaporudi" (when he comes back), as the English Readable does. "Kwake" in "kuja kwake" is a possessive and so takes the deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: taji ya fahari (L); taji tutakayoionea fahari (B); taji ya mshindi (R)
decisions.reason: "Taji" is used in Swahili both for a king's crown and for a winner's crown, so it serves for the victor's wreath (meaning decision). "Fahari" (pride) for the boasting word, as in 2 Corinthians 1:12, where the noun names proper pride.

decisions.reason: Here δόξα is the honor that comes to Paul from his work, not God's own glory: the Thessalonians are what he will rejoice in at Christ's coming (verse 19).
